facts.condition: A binary-input receiver’s information curve obeys one channel-independent continuity envelope when its Bernoulli input law is perturbed.

Balanced posterior representations yield a compact completion of receiver curves; discrete receiver laws can approach every completed curve uniformly, while an existing reflection relation can be retained.

Small uniform perturbations of the two receiver curves induce controlled rowwise perturbations in the accepted auxiliary constraint system, so a witness lying in the interior of every row remains feasible after sufficiently fine discretization; no boundary-optimum continuity follows.

assumptions: The predecessor constraint construction and discrete posterior representation incorporated by the builder remain valid.
Receiver curves use the canonical balanced-input normalization.
